title: ApexAI discovery - migration OpenAI -> Dedicated
summary: Discovery call for migration from OpenAI-hosted inference to Redwood Dedicated. Customer wants eval parity, lower per-token cost, predictable latency for production chat and embeddings, and private deployment options for regulated customers. Next steps: run a 2-week benchmark, share security and pricing docs, schedule a technical deep-dive focused on vLLM/TGI compatibility and canary rollout plan.
topics: Compatibility with vLLM/TGI and eval parity
Latency & cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 16:00 UTC | Duration 49m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, ApexAI), Raj Patel (Platform Eng), Nina Gomez (CTO)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood inference, joining me is Ethan our solutions engineer. uh quick intro round?
[00:15] Lena (ApexAI): hi lena here, head of ml at apexai, we own the chat and summarization work.
[00:22] Raj (ApexAI): raj platform engineer, i manage the infra side.
[00:26] Nina (ApexAI): nina, cto, i might jump in on infra/security questions.
[00:32] Maya: awesome. goal today is to understand your current stack and migration drivers from openai and talk about options - hosted vs dedicated vs private. Ethan will cover technical compatibility.
[00:45] Ethan (Redwood SE): hi all, quick agenda: current usage, perf/cost targets, eval parity with your prompts, and benchmarks with vllm/tgi stacks and dedicated offering.
[01:10] Lena: quick context - we currently use OpenAI for chat completions + embeddings. about 150M tokens/month now, spikes to 3x in marketing campaigns. latency matters for chat ui, target 200-400ms p50 for small prompts. cost is getting painful as we scale. also compliance requests for EU data residency and SOC2 reqs.
[01:40] Maya: got it. are you on any long-term contracts with openai or using pay-as-you-go?
[01:48] Lena: pay-as-you-go mostly, but we have committed credits for some customers. looking at dedicated to get predictable throughput and lower unit cost.
[02:05] Raj: also, our engineering team wants control over KV cache behavior - we run some prefixes locally using vllm right now for caching. compatibility with your runtime is a big Q for us.
[02:30] Ethan: good note on kv cache and vllm - our dedicated runtime supports standard kv cache semantics and we integrate with vllm and TGI model families, but we'll validate parity. sometimes names and model IDs shift - small transcribe issues in older docs - but we can map model variants.
[02:55] Maya: what about eval parity? do you have a benchmark set?
[03:05] Lena: yes we have a ~2k prompt test covering chat responses, safety, and hallucination metrics. we want near-100% parity for customer-facing flows.
[03:18] Ethan: great - we usually run that test on our hosted models and then on dedicated with same model binary or quantization profile to check regressions. small differences can happen with quantization or different kernel paths but we try to surface them.
[03:40] Nina: how do you handle quantization? we run int8 on vllm for cost reasons. concern is quality drop.
[03:50] Ethan: we have tested int8 and mixed precision quantization profiles. Redwood Optimize recommends quant configs per workload. for the pilot we can run both fp16 and int8 and show delta in evals.
[04:10] Raj: network - for dedicated private, is there a vpc peering or private link option? we need to avoid public egress for some customers.
[04:18] Maya: yes vpc peering and private link are supported; for private deployments we offer customer-managed networking and on-prem options.
[04:30] Lena: security checklist - SOC2, ISO, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations. do you have those docs?
[04:40] Maya: yes we have SOC2 and compliance pack, SSO with SAML, roles, and KMS integrations. we'll share the security dossier after the call.
[04:55] Ethan: one more infra note - for burst handling our dedicated pools support autoscaling and we have fallbacks to hosted for capacity overflow if you want hybrid.
[05:10] Nina: interesting. pricewise, what sort of uplift/discounts for reserved capacity?
[05:18] Maya: typical reserved committed discounts vary by commit; i'll send a pricing sheet. reserved gets you lower per-token and predictable latency SLOs.
[05:30] Lena: on the topic of compatibility - we use custom prompt templates and function calling currently via OpenAI-style APIs. will those APIs change with Redwood?
[05:42] Ethan: Redwood's API is similar to OpenAI in shape - chat, completions, embeddings, and function/tool calling. there are small differences in param names but we provide SDKs and migration guides. in dedicated/private we support pinning model versions and rollouts.
[06:05] Raj: when you say you support vllm - do you mean we can bring our own vllm wrappers, or you run vllm under the hood?
[06:14] Ethan: for Dedicated we run our optimized runtime; it can be configured to use vllm-like kernel paths and we've validated models commonly run on vllm/TGI. for private/on-prem we can collaborate on running your vllm stack.
[06:35] Lena: any customers who've migrated from OpenAI successfully?
[06:40] Maya: yes, a few - we've got case studies; i'll link two examples, one in healthtech and one in commerce - both migrated to Dedicated for cost and latency reasons.
[06:55] Nina: benchmarking - what does a benchmark engagement look like?
[07:02] Ethan: we typically run a 2-week pilot: 1) replicate your prompt set on our hosted infra to establish baseline, 2) run same evals on Dedicated with your quantization profiles and config, 3) collect token-level cost and latency metrics, 4) report regressions and a remediation plan.
[07:25] Raj: how do you instrument token-level cost - do you export token traces?
[07:30] Ethan: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and traces per route. we can export CSVs.
[07:40] Lena: timelines - if pilot looks good, how long to spin dedicated?
[07:46] Maya: for standard dedicated pools with reserved capacity it's typically 4-8 weeks depending on region and GPU family availability. private/on-prem can be longer.
[08:00] Nina: who owns data retention - if we choose dedicated, is customer data fully isolated?
[08:07] Maya: Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and data isolation controls; audit logs and retention policies are configurable. we'll cover specifics in the security doc.
[08:20] Lena: any gotchas with hallucinations or safety when switching runtime or quantization?
[08:28] Ethan: hallucination patterns can change slightly due to quantization or kernel changes. that's why we run the eval suite and check safety metrics. we also hook into regressions alerts.
[08:45] Raj: curious about endpoint latency under load - we saw p95 spikes on openai during traffic surges, how do you handle that?
[08:53] Ethan: Dedicated pools are provisioned for predictable throughput; you can define latency SLOs and autoscaling + burst capacity. plus smart routing can fallback to lower-cost variants or hosted during extreme conditions.
[09:10] Maya: let's walk through an example cost comparison quickly - assume 150M tokens/month, current openai cost approx X (redacted) - dedicated reserved shows ~40% lower unit costs in our modeled workloads.
[09:30] Lena: that 40% is attractive. are there egress fees or hidden costs?
[09:36] Maya: we include network egress estimates in the pricing sheet; for private deployments there could be different network charges depending on peering. we'll send detailed breakdown.
[09:50] Nina: on API compatibility, any risk of function call behavior differences? we've seen slight JSON schema differences when we tried another vendor.
[10:00] Ethan: we aim for OpenAI-style semantics but do test function calling specifically in the eval suite; we also support structured output. any function-calling edgecases we'll surface in the report.
[10:20] Lena: about model catalog - do you host Llama-family models, or rely on upstream vendors?
[10:27] Ethan: we host a curated catalog including Llama variants and other open models; we also verify performance profiles. if you have licensed models, we can onboard them into Dedicated.
[10:40] Raj: what about latency on large context windows? some of our summarization jobs use 8k-32k windows.
[10:48] Ethan: our runtime optimizes attention and kv cache management; for long-context workloads we recommend specific kernel and hardware combos - we'll include recommendations in the pilot plan.
[11:05] Maya: quick pause - any blockers so far?
[11:08] Lena: main blockers: 1) eval parity (we need confidence), 2) security docs, 3) cost model for reserved capacity.
[11:18] Maya: understood. we'll run the 2-week benchmark, share security docs and pricing sheet.
[11:25] Raj: do you have an SLA for latency?
[11:28] Maya: Dedicated includes SLA for uptime and we can agree on latency SLOs in enterprise contracts.
[11:35] Nina: curious about access controls - can we map our internal RBAC to Redwood roles?
[11:40] Ethan: yes SSO + SCIM and role mappings are supported.
[11:48] Lena: ok, one more question - we sometimes use TGI in-house; will Redwood support our TGI configs?
[11:55] Ethan: we validate TGI-based model families; for the pilot we can run your TGI config or an equivalent. compatibility validations are part of our tech-deep-dive.
[12:10] Maya: sounds good. we'll need a short statement of work for the pilot - can we confirm resource owners?
[12:18] Lena: i'll be the product owner, raj will be infra owner, nina is exec sponsor.
[12:24] Maya: perfect. next step - price sheet, security pack, schedule tech-deep-dive next week.
[12:32] Ethan: i'll also put together a benchmark plan template and share example results from similar migrations.
[12:40] Raj: timeline wise, we'd like pilot started within 2 weeks.
[12:45] Maya: doable - we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with proposed dates.
[12:50] Nina: one quick nit - do you support customer-managed KMS keys?
[12:55] Maya: yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM integration is supported for Private and some Dedicated configs.
[13:04] Lena: great. any concerns about data residency in EU for some customers?
[13:09] Maya: we have EU regions and private options; we'll note that in the SOW.
[13:18] Ethan: ok i think that's the major tech notes. we'll run a mapping of your prompt test to our eval harness.
[13:25] Maya: recap - action items and next steps.
[13:28] Lena: thanks all.

Notes: natural transcription artifacts present: occasional speaker overlaps and minor ASR errors (vllm transcribed as "V-L-L-M" in earlier notes).
